title: Sable and the Machine
premise: Lena Villalobos, a disgraced starship navigator, keeps the derelict beacon at Sable Station alive because it's the only thing that still answers to her name. When the freighter Meridian returns from deep space with its crew aged backward into children who remember a war that hasn't happened yet, Lena realizes her beacon has been receiving their distress calls for years — and deleting them on orders she never gave. The backups sleeping in her hold are copies of the Meridian's future crew, sent back as a warning. To deliver their message before the fleet's fragile truce expires, Lena must choose between exposing the conspiracy that erased her career and protecting the child-version of the man who betrayed her. She delivers the message, the truce holds by a single vote, and Lena finally lets the backups — and her guilt — go dark.
about_author: Zephyrine Villalobos is a former merchant marine radio operator who spent eleven years on deep-space relay stations before turning to fiction. Her stories about lonely beacons and impossible messages have appeared in three anthologies; this is her first novel.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Lena Villalobos, POV. Establishes Sable Station's decay and Lena's obsessive maintenance of an unauthorized beacon, plus the sealed hold of backups she refuses to open. Emotional beat: ritual as penance — she tends the machine because she cannot forgive herself.

chapters.title: Children in the Airlock
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. The freighter Meridian docks unbidden; its crew of nine emerges aged backward into children wearing adult memories in their eyes. One girl calls Lena by name. Emotional beat: uncanny dread curdling into recognition — something has come back wrong.

chapters.title: Manifest of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. The ship's logs show a voyage that never departed: dates from six years hence, signed with Lena's own authorization code. Emotional beat: vertigo — the past is being edited, and someone used her hands to do it.

chapters.title: What the Hold Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating Lena and the eldest child, Ivo, POV. Ivo insists the backups in Lena's hold are his crew — their future selves, transmitted back as a warning. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance between the woman who buried the past and the boy carrying the future.

chapters.title: Truce Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Fleet liaison Commander Osei, POV. Introduces the ceasefire expiring in nineteen days and the political factions who want the Meridian's arrival buried. Osei orders the children quarantined. Emotional beat: cold institutional logic pressing against human stakes.

chapters.title: Deleted Distress
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. She finds years of deleted distress transmissions from the Meridian in the beacon's shadow archives — suppressed by a command signature she recognizes: her old captain, Dario Reyes. Emotional beat: betrayal rekindled; the machine was complicit all along.

chapters.title: Ivo at Eight
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. A quiet chapter: the de-aged crew's memories fraying as childhood reasserts itself. Ivo fights to hold onto the message he was sent to deliver. Emotional beat: grief for a self dissolving in real time.

chapters.title: Reyes Arrives
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. Captain Dario Reyes boards Sable Station under diplomatic colors, older, decorated, and lying smoothly about the Meridian's 'salvage.' Emotional beat: the past walking through the door wearing medals — fear braided with fury.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days
chapters.summary: Osei, POV. Osei privately suspects Reyes but needs proof before the truce vote; he offers Lena immunity in exchange for the backups. Emotional beat: temptation — justice offered through the same machinery that wronged her.

chapters.title: The First Backup Wakes
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. Against every instinct, Lena wakes one backup: an adult Ivo, six years dead in her timeline, who confirms the coming war and names the weapon Reyes is building. Emotional beat: resurrection as violation — she gets truth at the cost of desecration.

chapters.title: Small Hands, Long Memory
chapters.summary: Ivo (child), POV. The children, sensing quarantine means erasure, sabotage the station's comms to force contact with the fleet press. Emotional beat: desperate agency — the smallest people making the loudest noise.

chapters.title: What Reyes Took
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. Flashback chapter: how Reyes framed Lena for the navigation failure that killed forty-one people, and why she signed the confession. Emotional beat: the full weight of inheritance — guilt passed down like debt.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Osei, POV. Reyes moves to seize the Meridian and scrub the children; Osei must choose between his career and warning Lena. Emotional beat: a decent man deciding the law is insufficient.

chapters.title: Dark Station
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. Reyes cuts Sable's power; Lena navigates the black station by memory and beacon-pulse to reach the hold first. Emotional beat: the navigator's craft as salvation — her disgrace becomes her advantage.

chapters.title: Two Ivos
chapters.summary: Lena and both Ivos, POV. Child and adult Ivo meet across the backup glass; the message can only be completed if both consent. Emotional beat: reconciliation with oneself — the book's thematic heart.

chapters.title: The Message
chapters.summary: Adult Ivo, POV. The full transmission: coordinates, casualty projections, and proof the war begins with a false-flag strike ordered by Reyes's faction. Emotional beat: terrible clarity — survival requires burning the man who built the future.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. With Osei jamming fleet countermeasures, Lena aims the forgotten beacon at the entire armada and sends everything. Emotional beat: catharsis — the machine nobody remembers commissioning becomes the most important transmitter in the system.

chapters.title: Reyes's Last Navigation
chapters.summary: Reyes, POV. Cornered, Reyes attempts to jump the Meridian out with the children aboard; Lena locks his helm using the beacon's guidance codes. Emotional beat: the betrayer undone by the systems he dismissed.

chapters.title: Vote at Armistice Point
chapters.summary: Osei, POV. The evidence reaches the fleet assembly hours before the truce expires; the vote extends the ceasefire and orders Reyes's arrest. Emotional beat: exhausted, hard-won hope — justice outside the law, ratified by it.

chapters.title: Letting Them Sleep
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. Adult Ivo asks to be shut down rather than live as a copy; the other backups follow. Lena powers down the hold herself. Emotional beat: mourning without regret — the price of survival paid willingly.

chapters.title: Decommissioning
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. The children are reunited with families; Lena declines reinstatement and instead takes stewardship of the beacon, now officially commissioned in the Meridian crew's names. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed — what was hidden becomes legacy.

chapters.title: Signal, Answered
chapters.summary: Lena, POV, epilogue. Months later, the beacon receives a faint reply from deep space — not the Meridian, something new. Lena smiles and opens a channel. Emotional beat: quiet wonder — survival was the beginning, not the end.
